Suresh Felix vs The Managing Director on 7 August, 2025

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) has been filed by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.886/2018 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Kottayam (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 28/12/2019.
The respondents herein are the respondents in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 23/06/2017 at about 06:15 a.m., while he was travelling as passenger in K.S.R.T.C. bus bearing registration no. KL-15/A 1258 and when he reached at Achikkal-Kuravilangadu, another K.S.R.T.C. bus bearing registration no. KL-15/A 1855 driven by the second respondent in a rash and negligent manner collided with the bus as a result of which he sustained 2025:KER:59413 grievous injuries.
3. The first respondent/owner and the second respondent/driver field written statement contending that the amount claimed was excessive.
4. The third respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the policy, but denying negligence on the part of the second respondent/driver.
5. Before the Tribunal, PW1 was examined and Exts.A1 to A10 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No oral or documentary evidence was adduced by the respondents.
Ext.X1 copy of muster roll was also marked.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the oral and documentary evidence and after hearing both sides,
found negligence on the part of the second respondent/driver of the offending bus resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 2,98,240/- together with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of the petition till the date of realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.

sentences.text: 7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides.

9. The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner - Loss of earnings It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that when 71,000/- was taken as the monthly income of the claim petitioner, the Tribunal committed a gross error in awarding an amount of 1,00,000/- only towards loss of earnings for a period of 83 days.
Therefore, he submits that the balance amount to which he is entitled may also be awarded by this Court.
9.1. The Tribunal as per the impugned Award has taken 71,000/- as the monthly income of the claim petitioner.
The materials on record show that he was on leave for 83 days on loss of pay.
Therefore, he will be entitled to an amount of 1,96,433/-.
Compensation for continuing or permanent disability 10.

The learned counsel for the claim petitioner quite persuasively submitted that as the permanent disability has been fixed at 2% as conceded by both sides, the Tribunal fixing the notional income as 8,000/- was quite unjustified and the same needs to be enhanced.
The learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer points out that no disability certificate had been produced.
That being the position, the claim petitioner was not entitled to any amount.
Despite the same, an amount of 17,280/- has been granted by the Tribunal and therefore, no interference or enhancement is called for.
11. Admittedly, the claim petitioner has not produced any disability certificate or any medical certificate to show the disability sustained pursuant to the accident.
Despite the same, on the basis of the concession made by both sides, the disability percentage is seen fixed as 2% .
When the functional disability is 2% only, there appears to be no reason why any further enhancement to the amount already granted is required.
Therefore, the argument on this aspect is rejected.

12. The impugned Award is modified to the following extent :
